headline: Trust, But Verify: Schools Press for Proof as AI Tools Multiply and Events Gear Up
thesis: From EdSurge's podcast on vetting AI features to Inside Higher Ed's usage data, the sector is asking what evidence backs the AI hype as EdTech Week and Tech Congress approach.
summary: EdSurge's latest "This Week" episode asks whether schools can trust AI features in edtech products, with EdReports' Courtney Allison on why the line between core and supplemental materials is disappearing. Inside Higher Ed's Instructure-based data finding that AI integration in higher ed is overhyped remains the lead higher-ed story, alongside coverage of AI reshaping student success and colleges embedding AI literacy (Agnes Scott, Bryn Mawr, DeVry). Brookings' task force continues to argue AI's risks currently outweigh its benefits for students unless the arc is bent, while Ed-Fi impact stories show real-time data driving results in Michigan, Texas and South Carolina. On the calendar: EdTech Week (Oct 13-15, Columbia Teachers College), 1EdTech's Technical Congress (Oct 19-21), and ISTE+ASCD's Scottsdale convening (Oct 19-20).
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 1, 2026 · Direct page fetches were blocked by the network proxy, so items come from search-indexed results and snippets; several sources had no new dated news, so evergreen items are listed with notes.
